_comment: Vermont Hobbies page. To add a hobby: copy any entry, append to the list — the page renders the two tiers automatically. tier: 'vermont' = only-really-works-here (top section), 'anywhere' = do-anywhere hobby with local hooks. Link types: shop | club | spot | guide (guide = internal page, relative URL). Every shop/club must be a real, currently operating Vermont (Burlington-area preferred; town named when it isn't) business — verify before adding. months: calendar months (1-12) the hobby is in season — in-season hobbies sort to the top of their tier with a badge; all 12 months = year-round (no badge).

hobbies.name: Skiing & riding
hobbies.what: The mountain is half an hour away, and "I ski after work" is a normal sentence here — Bolton's night lights make a hundred-day season possible on a day-job schedule.
hobbies.start: Get a used setup from OGE's gear basement or Skirack, then start with a Bolton night pass. Cochran's in Richmond is the tiny, cheap community hill where half of Burlington learned.

hobbies.name: Swimming holes & lake swims
hobbies.what: Between the lake beaches and the river holes, half of summer here is just deciding which water to get in after work.
hobbies.start: Check the swim statuses first (the lake occasionally says no), then do the classic: the roped swim beach at Red Rocks after work. The cliff area there is closed to jumping — the park is serious about it. Bolton Potholes is the river-hole field trip when you're ready.

hobbies.name: Backyard sugaring
hobbies.what: Tap the maples in your own yard when the nights still freeze and the days don't, and by Town Meeting Day you're boiling sap in the driveway like a real Vermonter.
hobbies.start: Two or three taps and a starter kit is plenty for a first season — Vermont Evaporator in Montpelier builds kits exactly for this. Watch a boil at Audubon's sugarhouse in March to see the whole arc first.

hobbies.name: Foraging
hobbies.what: Ramps in May, chanterelles in July, wild apples nobody picks in September — the woods around here genuinely feed you once you learn what you're looking at.
hobbies.start: Go out with someone who knows first: the Vermont Mycological Society leads walks all season, and The Mushroom Forager runs beginner forays out of Richmond. Then never tell anyone your spots.

hobbies.name: Ice fishing
hobbies.what: When Malletts Bay freezes, a small village of shanties appears on it — and the people out there are having a much better time than it looks from shore.
hobbies.start: Fish & Wildlife runs free intro clinics every winter with all the gear provided, and the last Saturday of January is Free Ice Fishing Day, no license needed. Bibens Ace in Colchester is on the state's bait dealer list when you're ready to fish for real.

hobbies.name: Disc golf
hobbies.what: Vermont is quietly one of the best disc golf states in the country, and Burlington keeps a free nine-hole course in the New North End to prove it.
hobbies.start: A starter set costs about what lunch does. Throw a round at Schifilliti Park after work; when you're hooked, the destination courses at Smugglers' Notch are an hour away.

hobbies.name: Sunset chasing
hobbies.what: The sun goes down over the Adirondacks across ten miles of open water, and people here genuinely plan their evenings around it.
hobbies.start: Check tonight's score on the sunset page, then be at Battery Park or the Waterfront Park swings twenty minutes before it drops. Winter ones are the underrated ones.

hobbies.name: Paddling the lake
hobbies.what: The lake is right there, and on a calm evening being out on it turns the whole city into a postcard you happen to live in.
hobbies.start: Rent a kayak or board right off the sand at North Beach to try it once, then take a real lesson at the Community Sailing Center — they teach kayak, SUP, and actual sailing on the waterfront.

hobbies.name: Hiking, mud season included
hobbies.season: Year-round, with an asterisk in April
hobbies.what: Camel's Hump and Mansfield are day trips, Philo is barely more than a lunch break — and the unwritten rule is you stay off the high trails in mud season so they're still there in June.
hobbies.start: Join a Green Mountain Club Burlington Section outing — they run hikes all year and you don't have to be a member. April belongs to the low stuff: Mt. Philo and Niquette Bay.

hobbies.name: Riding the causeway
hobbies.what: A rail causeway runs three miles into the middle of the lake, water on both sides, mountains on both horizons — the single best "why I live here" bike ride there is.
hobbies.start: Rent from Local Motion on the waterfront, ride the Island Line north through the New North End, and in summer catch the bike ferry across the cut to the Islands.

hobbies.name: Birding
hobbies.season: Year-round; May migration is the show
hobbies.what: The lake is a migration highway, so twice a year the birds come to you — and Delta Park, where the Winooski meets Champlain, is the front-row seat.
hobbies.start: Walk Delta Park's boardwalk with any pair of binoculars, then do a guided walk at the Audubon Center in Huntington. The Birds of Vermont Museum's 500 hand-carved birds are the field guide you walk through.

hobbies.name: Mountain biking
hobbies.what: Chittenden County is laced with volunteer-built singletrack — Saxon Hill, Sunny Hollow, Mud Pond — all of it maintained by the Fellowship of the Wheel, and all of it twenty minutes from downtown.
hobbies.start: Start on the flowy beginner loops at Catamount in Williston, where you can pay a day fee and just ride. Then join a Fellowship group ride or trail day — digging one afternoon of dirt is the fastest way into the scene.

hobbies.name: Cross-country skiing & snowshoeing
hobbies.what: When the snow lands, the same trails you hiked in September turn into a quiet second season — and the groomed centers at Catamount and Sleepy Hollow are closer than the ski resorts.
hobbies.start: Rent a classic setup at Catamount in Williston and do a lap after work — it's minutes from town and groomed all winter. After a storm, the Intervale and Red Rocks are the free in-city versions.

hobbies.name: Rowing & dragon boat
hobbies.what: Every summer week, crews row traditional wooden skiffs off Perkins Pier and dragon boats charge out of the sailing center — team sports where the playing field is Lake Champlain.
hobbies.start: The Maritime Museum's Wednesday-evening community row welcomes total beginners in six-person St. Ayles skiffs — just sign up for a seat. Want speed? Malia's dragon boat crews run beginner bootcamps.

hobbies.name: The 251 Club
hobbies.what: Since 1954, Vermonters have been quietly working the same checklist: visit all 251 of the state's towns and cities. It turns every free Saturday into an excuse for a drive.
hobbies.start: Join the club, print the checklist, and start knocking off the Chittenden County towns you've technically never actually stopped in. General stores and creemee stands count as visits — that's the whole point.

hobbies.name: Snowmobiling
hobbies.what: VAST grooms 4,700 miles of trail across the state — a whole winter highway system that only exists because volunteer clubs and generous landowners keep it open.
hobbies.start: You ride legally by joining VAST through a local club, which is also where you'll find the people, the trail wisdom, and often a used sled. Guided intro tours at the resorts let you try it before buying anything.

hobbies.name: Board games
hobbies.what: This town supports a proper game shop and a board-game café within a few blocks of each other, which tells you everything about what winter is like.
hobbies.start: Quarterstaff on Bank Street will match a game to your exact group; The Boardroom lets you play from a wall of 700 over a beer. Standing game nights live on the clubs page.

links.name: Game nights on the clubs page

hobbies.name: Skating & pickup hockey
hobbies.what: Every Vermont kid can skate, and the city rink at Leddy Park is where the grown-ups quietly catch up — public skates, stick-and-puck, learn-to-skate, all cheap.
hobbies.start: Public skate at Leddy Arena runs a few bucks and rentals are five. Got your own skates? Kevin Smith Sports in South Burlington will put a real edge on them.

hobbies.name: Reading & book clubs
hobbies.what: Used at Crow, new at Phoenix, free at Fletcher — three good answers to "where's my next book" within a five-minute walk of each other.
hobbies.start: A Fletcher Free card costs nothing and takes five minutes. Then pick a book club off the clubs page — there are several, and they actually meet.

links.name: Book clubs on the clubs page

hobbies.name: Climbing
hobbies.what: Petra Cliffs has been Burlington's climbing living room for decades — half the gym seems to know each other, and they'll rope you in fast.
hobbies.start: Book an intro class at Petra — belay basics in one evening — then let their guides take you outside when the rock dries out.

hobbies.name: Running
hobbies.season: Year-round if you're honest about layers
hobbies.what: The bike path along the lake means your default easy run comes with a water view, and the run-club scene here is genuinely social — most end at a brewery.
hobbies.start: Get fitted at Skirack, then just show up to a club run — Friday evenings at Foam is the famous one, and nobody cares about your pace.

links.name: Run clubs on the clubs page

hobbies.name: Pottery & making things
hobbies.what: Between BCA's clay studio and the Generator makerspace, Pine Street will teach you to make almost anything with your hands.
hobbies.start: BCA's intro wheel classes are the classic first move — twelve wheels, real teachers, your own lopsided mugs. Generator's tool trainings open up wood, metal, laser, and sewing shops.

hobbies.name: Knitting & fiber arts
hobbies.season: Cast on in October, wear it by February
hobbies.what: A Vermont winter is the reason knitting was invented, and there's a real yarn shop ten minutes down Shelburne Road that treats it that way.
hobbies.start: Must Love Yarn will set a total beginner up with needles, wool, and patience — then come back for their open craft hours on Wednesday evenings and Sunday afternoons.

hobbies.name: Film photography
hobbies.season: Year-round; golden hour is over the lake
hobbies.what: A real camera shop survives on Main Street — used bodies, fresh film, in-house developing — and this city hands you a postcard sunset to shoot most weeks.
hobbies.start: LeZot will put a working film camera in your hands for less than you think and develop what you shoot. Best of it ends up on our community photos page — send yours.

hobbies.name: Homebrewing
hobbies.season: Brew day is a winter Saturday
hobbies.what: You live in the state with the most breweries per capita — brewing your own is practically a civic duty, and the continuing education is a walk down Pine Street.
hobbies.start: Start with a one-gallon kit ordered online, then find the local brewers: Vermont's homebrew clubs trade yeast, recipes, and honest feedback, and the annual homebrew competitions are where you'll meet all of them.

hobbies.name: Gardening
hobbies.season: Plan in March, plant after Memorial Day
hobbies.what: Gardener's Supply started here, the Intervale is a whole valley of growing, and the city rents garden plots for the yardless — this is not a town where you garden alone.
hobbies.start: Get on the community garden list early — the city's 14 sites fill up fast every spring — and let the Intervale garden center answer your beginner questions; it's what they're for.

hobbies.name: Playing music
hobbies.what: This is a music town out of proportion to its size, and the distance between "I play a little" and "I played out last night" is unusually short here.
hobbies.start: Radio Bean's long-running open mic is the on-ramp everyone uses. Looking for people to play with? The clubs page keeps a music section.

links.name: Music groups on the clubs page

hobbies.name: Yoga
hobbies.what: Burlington's yoga anchor is a nonprofit — donation-based, scholarship-friendly, and busy — which changes who you meet on the next mat over.
hobbies.start: Drop into any beginner class at Sangha, Pine Street or the Old North End. Suggested donation is ten to fifteen bucks; pay what you can.

hobbies.name: Trivia nights
hobbies.what: Ask r/burlington how to meet people here and the top answer is usually "wanna join my trivia team?" — there's a free quiz somewhere in the area almost every night of the week, and teams genuinely adopt strangers.
hobbies.start: Mondays it's Trivia with Craig Mitchell at the Monkey House, Wednesdays it's Citizen Cider's pub — and every other Thursday the Btown Brief crew plays at Four Quarters in Winooski. Come say hi; we always need one more.

hobbies.name: Rec-league sports
hobbies.what: Kickball, cornhole, volleyball, even popdarts — GameOnVT runs casual adult leagues where signing up alone is normal and the team you're assigned to becomes your new friend group.
hobbies.start: Pick a sport at your actual skill level (cornhole exists for a reason), register solo as a free agent, and let the schedule do the socializing. Seasons run all year, indoors when it snows.

hobbies.name: Pickleball
hobbies.season: April–October outside; gyms carry the winter
hobbies.what: The fastest-growing hobby in the county, and the city built real courts for it — the Szymanski Park courts stay busy from thaw to frost, and open play means you just show up.
hobbies.start: Borrow a paddle and join open play at Szymanski Park in the New North End — rotating in with strangers is the culture, not an imposition. GameOnVT runs leagues when you want structure.

hobbies.name: Contra & swing dancing
hobbies.what: Contra is the sober, sweaty, 200-year-old New England tradition that r/burlington keeps calling the best way to meet people here — and the swing scene runs weekly on top of it.
hobbies.start: Show up to a Queen City Contras dance fifteen minutes early for the beginner walkthrough — no partner or experience needed, sliding-scale admission. Vermont Swings teaches Tuesday-night lessons at the Champlain Club.

hobbies.name: Improv & standup
hobbies.what: Vermont Comedy Club isn't just a place to watch comedy — its classes have quietly become one of the friendliest communities in town, the kind reddit recommends to lonely newcomers by name.
hobbies.start: Take Improv 101 — it's built for people who have never performed and are mildly terrified. Student showcases mean you'll be on a real stage, gently, sooner than you think.

hobbies.name: Sauna & cold plunge
hobbies.what: Two wood-fired-hot saunas and a cold plunge sit on a deck by the lake behind Hula — the closest thing Burlington has to Nordic bath culture, and the correct answer to February.
hobbies.start: Book a session at Savu on the waterfront and do the full circuit: heat, plunge, Adirondack chair, repeat. Going right after a cold-water lake dip season ends is how locals stretch swimming into winter.

hobbies.name: D&D & Magic
hobbies.what: Between weekly Magic nights, Pokémon events, and open D&D tables, the area's game stores run a standing calendar that makes "I play tabletop games" a social life, not a solitary one.
hobbies.start: Vermont Gaming Academy on Dorset Street runs card nights and keeps play space for tabletop and D&D; Quarterstaff downtown hosts events too and will match you to a system. Just tell the counter you're new — recruiting players is what they do.

hobbies.name: Pinball
hobbies.what: A member-run co-op in South Burlington keeps three dozen machines — Addams Family to brand-new releases — in tournament shape, and opens the doors to everyone twice a week.
hobbies.start: Show up on a Wednesday or Friday open-play night: flat rate at the door, all machines on free play, regulars happy to explain why the older games are the good ones. Leagues when you're hooked.

hobbies.name: Volunteering
hobbies.what: The most upvoted friend-making advice on r/burlington isn't a bar or an app — it's volunteering, because working next to someone for a cause you both picked skips the small talk entirely.
hobbies.start: Browse United Way of Northwest Vermont's volunteer listings and pick something recurring rather than one-off — the regulars are the community. Green Up Day in May is the whole state doing it at once.

hobbies.name: Stargazing
hobbies.season: Year-round; winter skies are the clearest
hobbies.what: Get twenty minutes east of the city glow and Vermont's night sky still actually performs — and the state's astronomical society has been showing people around it since 1963.
hobbies.start: Go to a Vermont Astronomical Society public star party before buying anything — looking through a dozen members' telescopes beats owning one bad one. Binoculars and a dark pullout on a moonless night are a legitimate start.

hobbies.name: Pool & darts
hobbies.what: Vermont's only true billiards hall is hiding on San Remo Drive — ten full-size nine-foot tables, dart boards, and league nights that give a weekly game its own built-in crowd.
hobbies.start: Walk into Vermont Pool and Bar any evening and get a table — no membership, no pretense. When you're shooting regularly, ask about joining a league night; that's where the regulars come from.
